corpus_item: RI-MAG03 §B, §C (the soul-gem ruling), §D (the eleven sanctioned breakages)
note: Enchanting is the caster's SUSTAIN. Focus never regenerates (RI-MAG01 §A), so an enchanted item — with its own charge pool, refilled from soul gems — is the only renewable magic in the game. That is why the gem economy is load-bearing and why seam S15 has to be defended here rather than assumed.

no_enchant_skill.reason: RI-PRG03 ships exactly 19 skills; a 20th would invalidate its §3 event budget and RI-PRG02's 27-earned-attribute-point arithmetic. Enchanting is gated by the relevant SCHOOL skill and by WHO is doing it, which makes it a social and geographic system rather than a grind.

enchanters.name: Yourself
enchanters.note: Free. You pay in the gem and the item.

enchanters.name: The Stone Wastes recluse
enchanters.note: One, quest-gated, in the Stone Wastes. The Telvanni-analogue.

spellwright_note: Four in the world, and walking to one is part of the cost (RI-MAG03 §A, S7). A single spellwright in the starting town would make spellmaking a menu and undermine S7's argument that distance is content.

constant.note: The ×18 is what stops the endgame being a walking permanent-buff statue. Softening it to ×8 puts six permanent buffs on every late character and the Focus reservoir stops mattering (RI-MAG03 'How we lose').

grades.name: The Unfilling Stone
grades.note: MB-9. Safe ONLY because SG-3 and SG-4 already closed the money loop: with no path from enchantment to gold, an infinite gem buys convenience, not economy.

downgrade_on_respawn.rule: A respawned creature yields a soul ONE GRADE LOWER than its first death, floored at `petty`. Soul grade is a property of an INDIVIDUAL, not of an archetype.

soul_gems.npc_soul_rule: `soul_trap` on anything with a dialogue record does NOTHING and the Focus is still spent. Exactly one exception exists in the game and it is a main-quest artifact whose use is the transgression the plot is about.

SG_1.clause: A soul gem never contains xul-teekh.
SG_1.mechanised_as: No function in game/src/sim/magic/** reads or writes the souls quantity. Killing a creature yields its full sap-debt whether or not you also trapped it; soul-trapping does not reduce, replace, convert, increase or substitute for your souls in either direction.
SG_1.test: grep every gem/enchant/recharge path for `souls` — assert zero reads and zero writes.

SG_2.clause: A gem's contents are denominated in `charge`, and `charge` has exactly two sinks: enchanting an item, and recharging one.

SG_3.clause: A filled soul gem may not be sold, at any price, by anyone, ever.
SG_3.sell_value_note: `null`, not `0`. `null` means there is no transaction here; `0` would mean it is worthless, which it emphatically is not. An Argonian merchant will not touch one. The smugglers who do buy them are not a merchant — they are a quest.

SG_4.clause: An enchantment adds full value on purchase and zero value on sale.
SG_4.mechanised_as: sell price of an enchanted item = sell price of its unenchanted base. Between SG-3 and SG-4 there is no path from magic to gold, which is the whole requirement.

SG_5.clause: Grand and greater souls are hand-placed, and filling is not farmable.
SG_5.mechanised_as: 22 greater and 12 grand fillable sources; downgrade-on-respawn above.

SG_6.clause: Root-theft is tracked, and it costs you socially, never mechanically in a fight.

consequences.idiom: RI-LOR05's taint idiom — the player is shown, never told

SG_6.ui_rule: RI-LOR05 §3: they should not be told; they should be shown, repeatedly, and left to work it out. A tooltip explaining the soul-gem penalty is a defect.

breakage_register.what: Levitate/slowfall into a region you have no business in
breakage_register.test: levitate from an R2 vantage into R5; FAIL if the crossing is blocked, teleported back or fenced
Security 40 + fortify_skill +40 opens a tier-5 lock; FAIL if it refuses or if a base-skill-only evaluation appears anywhere

breakage_register.what: Commissioning a spell no designer authored, including one you cannot cast
breakage_register.test: build a 3-effect spell absent from spells.json, buy it, cast it; FAIL if any legal combination is refused
steal an owned item behind a barred window from outside; FAIL if the interaction is range-clamped to melee

breakage_register.what: Frenzy as an indirect murder weapon
breakage_register.test: frenzy an NPC into a lethal fight; FAIL if the death is unattributed, the target immune, or the world state reverts

breakage_register.what: Bound weapon as an early-game power spike
breakage_register.test: conjure at level 8 and clear an R2 encounter; FAIL if the weapon scales, upgrades or is nerfed to parity

breakage_register.what: Drain Health self-cast to pass a threshold
breakage_register.test: self-cast drain_health, cross a max-HP-gated trigger; FAIL if self-targeting is blocked or the trigger reads base HP

breakage_register.what: Enchantment stacking to reach a magnitude you cannot cast
breakage_register.test: equip three constant items and measure the summed effect; FAIL if stacking is blocked outright (a clamp is not a block)

breakage_register.what: The Unfilling Stone as an infinite enchanting engine
breakage_register.test: fill, enchant, refill 20 times; FAIL if the stone is consumed or capped, or the items become sellable

breakage_register.what: Paralysis/demoralise as a total fight bypass
breakage_register.test: paralyse an R4 group and reach the far exit without a kill; FAIL if any enemy is paralysis-immune by flag or the exit is combat-locked

breakage_register.what: Opening a quest door before you were told it existed
breakage_register.test: open_lock a quest-flagged door at stage 0; FAIL if the lock is unpickable-until-flagged or the interior is unloaded

anti_exploit_cross_rule: RI-MAG03 §D, binding on all of 25-magic: no new anti-exploit hard fail may be added anywhere in this area without naming the MB entry it leaves open.

gates.rule: You may only combine effects you already own a spell for. You cannot invent `paralyse` by naming it.
max_effects = min(5, 1 + floor(highest relevant school skill / 25))
Your school skill must be >= the tier requirement of the RESULTING spell, evaluated per effect's school. A two-school spell is gated by both.
gates.behaviour: Made and sold; UNATTUNABLE until the skill is reached (RI-PRG03 §6).

non_refusals.behaviour: Made and sold. The UI shows the number and shows your maximum. Uncastable until WILLPOWER catches up, and that is a legitimate goal to have.
Clamped to the max, and the clamp is shown.
Forced to 0, and the forcing is shown.
Forced to 0, and the forcing is shown.

non_refusals.case: two effects whose combination is nonsense
non_refusals.behaviour: Made. Nonsense is the player's business. Nothing in this system adjudicates taste.

spellmaking.no_whitelist: There is no list of designer-approved combinations anywhere in this build. A whitelist is an automatic fail of RI-MAG03. The four gates above are the only things that can refuse, and three of them state a number.
spellmaking.no_failure_roll: There is no spell-failure chance and no cast-failure roll anywhere in this system. Morrowind had both; both are deleted by S1 and the deletion is a ruling, not an oversight.

w1_14_r4_note: W1-14 ROUND 4 — THE SEVEN IDS BELOW ARE NOW PEOPLE. Until this round `enchanters[]` and `spellwrights[]` were a foreign key to nobody: no record in `game/data/npcs/**` carried any of these ids, so the whole spell-making system had exactly one caller in the build and it was `window.__HARNESS` (round-3 verdict §13, GAP-W1-magic-spellmaking-has-no-world-side-surface). `game/data/npcs/spellwrights.json` is the seven people. A record's `spellwright` field names a row of `spellwrights[]` and is what `Engine._commissionOpens()` resolves to open a counter; its `enchanter` field names a row of `enchanters[]`. `spellwright_note` below is still the rule and is still enforced by the data: four of the seven write spells, and the other three say so and name the town that does. THE ENCHANTING COUNTER IS NOT BUILT — `enchantQuote` still has one caller and it is the harness, and that half of the gap is open.
